# Kariyer

## Veteriner Teknikeri#

Tam zamanlı · Levent, Beşiktaş / İstanbul

Kum Ada Veteriner Onkoloji, Levent'te kedi ve köpeklerde kanser tanısı ve tedavisine odaklanan bir veteriner onkoloji merkezidir. Ekibimize tam zamanlı bir veteriner teknikeri arıyoruz.

### Yapılacak işler#

  * Muayene ve tedavi uygulamalarında veteriner hekimlere yardımcı olmak
  * Kan ve numune alımı, laboratuvar tahlillerinin hazırlanması
  * Röntgen ve ultrason çekimlerinde hasta hazırlığı
  * Operasyon ve anestezi hazırlığı, operasyon sonrası hasta takibi
  * Kemoterapi uygulamalarında hekime destek
  * Malzeme, sterilizasyon ve kayıt takibi

### Aradığımız nitelikler#

  * Laborant ve Veteriner Sağlık ön lisans programı ya da ilgili bir bölümden mezun olmak
  * Kedi ve köpeklerle sakin ve özenli çalışabilmek
  * Ekip çalışmasına yatkın olmak

### Çalışma koşulları#

  * Tam zamanlı, haftalık 45 saat
  * Yemek ve yol desteği
  * Ücret görüşmede konuşulur.

### Başvuru#

Özgeçmişinizi "Veteriner Teknikeri Başvurusu" konu başlığıyla info@adapoliclinic.com adresine gönderebilirsiniz. Sorularınız için bizi 0212 324 67 32 numarasından arayabilirsiniz.

# Feasibility and clinical safety of cytokine-activated anti-tumor lymphocytes infusion in dogs with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a pilot study

## Abstract

### Background

Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common histologic subtype of lymphoma in dogs. Although using cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine and prednisone (CHOP) chemotherapy is the standard treatment, outcomes remain suboptimal, emphasizing the need for novel therapeutic strategies.

### Hypothesis/Objectives

Evaluate the feasibility and potential therapeutic benefit of adoptive immunotherapy using ex vivo-expanded cytokine-activated anti-tumor lymphocytes (CATLs) in dogs with DLBCL treated using CHOP chemotherapy and an autologous tumor vaccine.

Colorado State University Veterinary Teaching Hospital · USA

Active - Recruiting

The protocol combines autologous engineered CAR T cells with oral verdinexor; radiation therapy is optional. Dogs may not have received prior chemotherapy or radiation. CSU lists recruitment through December 31, 2028; final neurologic and anesthesia eligibility requires study-team prescreening.

### Personalized mRNA-LNP immunotherapy for canine malignant tumors

PETcura (宝科雅) multicenter IIT · China

Recruiting — limited enrollment

What is being offered: Official study page updated 2026-08-15. Exploratory multicenter IIT for canine malignant tumors using fresh tumor plus paired adjacent normal tissue for >=50G RNA sequencing, neoantigen selection and personalized mRNA-LNP immunotherapy. T-cell lymphoma and brain tumors are explicitly excluded and therefore are not mapped to this record. Requires histologic or cytologic confirmation, age >=2 years, generally weight >=5 kg (smaller dogs may be individually assessed), fresh tumor and paired normal tissue obtainable at surgery; dogs already operated may still be considered if tissue was correctly frozen. Also requires adequate performance status/labs and successful LNP tolerance testing. Excludes recent chemotherapy/radiation/high-dose corticosteroids within 2 weeks, severe infection/autoimmune disease/immunodeficiency, pregnancy/lactation, and expected survival <6 months. 
Contact: University of Minnesota Clinical Investigation Center — 612-624-2485; Canine Brain Tumor Program clinical-trials coordinator Sara Pracht

## Abstract

This review summarizes the findings of veterinary clinical trials on immunogene therapy published between 2017 and 2024. Various tumor types, including melanoma (canine and feline), mastocytoma (canine), mammary adenocarcinoma (canine), osteosarcoma (canine), and sarcoid (equine), were treated using diverse strategies. Non-viral vectors were predominantly used to deliver genes encoding tumor-associated antigens, cytokines, or suicide enzymes. Among these non-viral methods, electrotransfer was the most commonly employed technique for introducing therapeutic genes into cells. Generally, these procedures resulted in minimal or no adverse side effects, and treated animals often showed significant improvements, such as enhanced quality of life, delayed or suppressed tumor recurrence or metastasis, and increased survival times. Some of these innovative approaches hold great potential as adjunct therapies to standard treatments. The promising outcomes from immunogene therapy studies in companion animals strongly support their application in veterinary oncology and provide valuable preclinical data (including safety assessments and proof-of-concept studies) for analogous human clinical trials.
